FOREWORD This Indian Standard ( Part 1 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 15 July 19g9, after the draft finalized by the Physical Methods of Test Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile Division Council. This standard was first published in 1970 as Part 6 covering terminology, and has been revised with a view to include some new terms and also to modify definition of the terms which already existed in the earlier version. This standard has been prepared with various interpretations of definition of standard forms a part of the series of cords and tyre cord warpsheets made standards covered in this series. a view to eliminate ambiguity or confusion arising from terms commonly used in tyre cord industry and trade. This standards under the title `Methods of test for tyre yarns, from man-made fibres' and covers terms used in different

PART ( 1 DEFINITION OF TERMS

First Revision)
2.7 Construction

1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard ( Part 1) defines various terms used in the testing of tyre yarns, cords and tyre cord warpsheets made from man-made fibres. 2 DEFINITIONS A 2.1 Adhesion The property of treated tyre yarns or cords by It is which they tend to adhere to the rubber. expressed in terms of force ( N ) for a fixed cord linear density or in force per unit width ( N/25 mm or kN/m ). 2.2 Air Wicking along or The passage of air longitudinally through yarns in a fabric that has been encased and cured in rubber or other elastomer, that is, air permeability in the plane of the fabric. B 2.3 Bow The greatest distance measured parallel to the selvedges, between a weft yarn and a straight line drawn between the points at which this Bow may be expressyarn meets the selvedges. ed directly in millimetres or as a percentage of the width of the fabric at that point. 2.4 Breaking Load The maximum tensile force observed during a test in which the specimen is stretched until it breaks. It is commonly expressed in newtons, centinewtons or millinewtons. C 2.5 Commercial Moisture Regain The agreed value to be be added to the mass of a defined material ( after drying it using prescibed methods ) in order to obtain its commercial mass, linear density, or mass per unit area. It is expressed as a percentage of the mass of the dried material. 2.6 Condition To bring a sample or specimen to moisture equilibrium for testing.

The geometrical 2.8 Creep

configuration

of a cord.

The increase in length of a specimen caused by the application of a continuing load or force under specified conditions. Creep is usually expressed as a percentage of the initial specimen length. D 2.9 Denier A unit of yarn number which is numerically equa1 to the number of grams per 9 000 metres of yarn. 2.10 Dip
A material applied adhesion to rubber.

to a textile to improve its

2.11 Dip Pick-Up The amount of dip present in the specimen. It is expressed as the percentage of mass of the oven-dry, dip-free specimen. 2.12 Dipping The process of impregnating a textile with a compound to improve its adhesion to rubber. E 2.13 Elongation The increase in length of a specimen during a tensile test expressed in units of length, for example, millimetres. 2.14 Elongation Percent The increase in length of a specimen during a tensile test expressed as a percentage of the nominal gauge length.
NOTE - In a tensile test, the elongation precent is calculated on the basis of the nominal gauge length of pre-tensioned specimen.

2.15 Elongation at Break The elongation produced by the breaking force ( that is, the maximum force applied during the determination of breaking strength ). 1

IS

4910 ( Part 1) : 1989 2.26 Load at Specified Elongation The load or force required to produce a specified or pre-determined percentage elongation of a tyre yarn or cord. It is expressed in newtons. M

2.16Elongation at Specified Load, Percent
The increase in length of a specimen at a certain desired load during a tensile test, expressed as a percentage of the nominal gauge length. 2.17 Ends Warp threads, usually of tyre cord. The ends per decimetre are the number of cords per decimetre of width. F 2.18 Filament Elementary continuous constituent of yarn.

2.27Mass

4

Gross Mass

The total mass of a consignment, case, roll or sample, including the mass of packing materials, containers and of supports, such as, cones and bobbins and shell rolls.

2.19 Filament Yarn A yarn composed of continuous bled with or without twist. 2.20 Finish a) Verb, the process of impregnating yarns with a substance to facilitate further processing. b) Noun, the substance used for finishing. H 2.21 Heat Degradation The drop in breaking load of tyre yarn or cord on exposure to an elevated temperature for a predetermined time. It is expressed as a percentage of breaking load of the conditioned specimen. 2.22 Heat Shrinkage The maximum decrease in length of yarn or cord when exposed to an elevated temperature under a pre-tension, it is expressed as a percentage of the nominal gauge length. 2.23 Heat Shrinkage Force The maximum force developed in the yarn or cord of fixed length when exposed to an elevated temperature. It is expressed as force per unit linear density, gltex or g/denier. I 2.24 Industrial Yarn A yarn usually of high tenacity, produced with or without twist and intended for applications in which functional properties are of primary importance; for example, in reinforcing material in polymeric products ( tyres, belting hoses ), protective coverings, ropes, nets, twines, filter and sail-cloth. L 2.25 Linear Density The mass per unit length. It is expressed tex or its multiples or sub-multiples. filament assem-

b)

Tare Mass

The mass of all external and internal packing materials of a case, roll or other type of containers including the mass of bobbins, tubes, etc.
Net c> Mass

The difference between the gross mass and the tare mass determined at the same time. d) Oven Dry Mass The mass of a samnle of textile material dried to substantially constant mass in an oven maintained at 105 f 3�C and supplied with air at standard atmospheric conditions ( 65 f 2 percent relative humidity and 27 & 2 "C temperature ).
Commercial e> Mass For undipped yarns and cords, 1)

2)

the sum of oven-dry mass and the mass corresponding to the commercial moisture regain. For dipped cords, the sum of oven-dry mass and the mass corresponding to commercial moisture regain for the textile plus an increase for dipping.

f) Invoiced Mass The mass used for billing. 2.28 Moisture Equilibrium The condition reached by a sample at a closely defined temperature and relative humidity when the net difference between the amount of moisture absorbed and the amount desorbed as indicated by a change in mass, shows no trend and becomes insignificant. 2.29 Moisture Equilibrium for Testing A textile material is in moisture equilibrium with the ambient atmosphere when it does not exchange water with this atmosphere; its mass then remains constant as long as the experiment is carried out in an unchanged atmosphere. For moisture equilibrium must be test purposes, reached by absorption starting from a relatively low moisture content.

IS 2.30 Moisture Regain The amount of moisture in a specimen determined under prescribed conditions, and express: ed as the percentage of oyen dry mass of the specimen. 2.31 Monofilament A single filament with or without twist. N 2.32 Nominal Gauge Length The length of a specimen under specified pretension, measured from nip to nip of the jaws of the holding lamps in their starting positions. P 2.33 Package A length or lengths of yarn in a form suitable for use, handling, storing or shipping. Packages may be unsupported, such as, balls, skeins or cakes or supported, such as, beams, bobbins, cops, cones, pirns, spools or tubes. 2.34 Plying
The operation of assembling two or more single yarns of the same length maintained under same tension.

4910 ( Part 1) :1989

T 2.39 Tab ( or Header ) Closely woven end portions 2.40 Tabby A full-width sample of tyre cord, usually 1 metre long, with two tabs at its ends to enable its removal from the roll. 2.41 Tenacity The ratio of breaking load to the linear density of the unstrained specimen, usually expressed in centinewtons per tex. 2.42 Tex The primary unit in a system of units expressing the universal count of yarn ( see Note ); the mass in grams of one kilometre of yarn.
NOTE - This system is also intended to be used for expressing the mass per unit length of fibres and other textile products, such as, ropes and rovings.
The following multiple and submultiple units may be used to avoid large numbers and small fractions, respectively: 1 ktex ( kilotex ) = 1 000 tex 1 mtex ( millitex) = 0'001 tex.

of a tyre cord roll.

2.35 Pre-Tension The initial force applied to remove kinks and crimp when preparing a specimen for test, and used to establish the nominal gauge length. S 2.36 Selvedge The woven edge portion of a fabric parallel to the warp. It may be of similar construction as the body of the fabric or differ from it in construction, weave or end spacing.
NOTE - Closed selvedges usually have an increased warp end density at the edges than in the body of the fabric; cut ( leno ) selvedges are usually formed by weaving with projectile weaving machines. The leno ends are to prevent the selvedge ends from falling out of the fabric after the picks have been cut; and auxiliary selvedge is necessary until the weft has been cut.

2.43 Thickness The distance between the upper and lower surface of a textile measured under a specified pressure; for tyre cords, this is measured as the average thickness of a group of parallel tyre cords. 2.44 Twist The a> number of turns about its axis per unit of length existing in a yarn based on the nominal gauge length before untwisting. It is usually expressed in turns per metre ( turns/m ). It may also be expressed as turns per centimetre ( turns/cm >.

2.37 Sewn Splice The term ( see 2.38 stitch on ( see Fig. used for sewn joints in tyre cord trade, ). This is made by applying a zig-zag two cord ends lying side by side 1).

The amount of twist in a cord made from two or more single yarns, it is based on the initial length of a cord specimen and is usually expressed in turns per metre.

2.38 Splice The joining of two ends of yarn or cord.

The twist in yarn due to which its spirals are in line with the central portion of the letter S, when the yarn is held in a vertical position ( see Fig. 2 ).

The latter merely serve to hold the cord in position for processing. W 2.47 Wet Contractile Force The maximum force developed in yarn or cord of fixed length when immersed in water. It is expressed as force per unit linear density ( newton/tex:).
FIG. 3 Z-TWIST Y

2.45 Tyre Cord A particular construction of filaments or fibres of cotton, rayon, polyamide, polyester, or other suitable fibres, used as the structural reinforcement of pneumatic tyres. 2.46 Tyre Cord Warpsheet A planar textile structure consisting of tyre cord

2.48 Yarn A continuous strand of textile fibres or filaments with or without twist, suitable for plying, knitting, braiding, weaving or otherwise intertwining to form a textile and product. Varieties include single yarn, plied yarn cabled yarn cord, thread, fancy yarn, etc.

I 1 Standard Mark
The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to Details of conditions under which a licence for the use that standard as a further safeguard. of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
